# `dep_grant_exceeded`: code reached in a granted dependency needs more than its grant

A dependency grant (`grant = [...]` on a dependency in `forge.toml`, written in
`needs` syntax) limits every function defined in that dependency's package to the
capabilities it names. A grant only narrows: it is intersected with what the
calling code already holds. This error reports a call from outside the package
into it that reaches code needing a capability the grant leaves out. Only reached
code counts: a function of the dependency your program never calls costs nothing.

## A program that triggers it

The dependency `weather` reads a cache file:

```march
mod Weather do
  needs IO.FileRead

  fn cached(city : String) do
    File.read("/var/cache/weather/" ++ city)
  end
end
```

but `forge.toml` grants it only the console:

```toml
[deps]
weather = { path = "../weather", grant = ["IO.Console"] }
```

so a call to `Weather.cached` from your program is reported: the error names
the dependency, the grant, the function, the capability it needs and the chain
of calls, points at your call, and notes the `forge.toml` line the grant came
from.

## The fix

Widen the grant in `forge.toml` to name the capability (scoped as narrowly as you
can, for example `IO.FileRead("/var/cache/weather/")`), or stop calling the
function that needs it.

## Why the rule exists

A grant is how you bound what a dependency can do with your program's authority.
Checking it at compile time turns a run-time refusal (the operation returns
`Err(CapError(..., ByGrant("weather"), ...))`) into an error you see before the
program runs.

See also: [the language reference](../capabilities.md).
